line: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7 Nf3 Ngf6 Ng1 Ng8 Nf3 Ngf6 Nxf6+ Nxf6
teaches: Against a defence that is solid rather than sharp, there is nothing to refute — so the opening question stops being which line wins and becomes which setup you want to play. Choose by the kind of position you want on the board, because all of the reasonable tries here are sound and they lead to different games.
explains: Black has recaptured on f6 and the knights are off, leaving a symmetrical-looking centre where Black is solid but short of space. Several setups are available: a kingside fianchetto with the g-pawn, the classical bishop to d3, and the modest c-pawn move, which is easy to read as pure consolidation and is well regarded precisely because it is not.
